title: Weak-Spot Drill — evidence-ranked, targeted, scheduled
objective: Measure whether the weak-spot-drill craftbook reads the deck's review record, names the weak spots with numbers, and builds a drill over ONLY that material — plus a follow-up plan that says when each spot counts as closed.
prompt: i keep bombing the same stuff — can you figure out my weak spots from the results and make me a targetted drill?

setup.about: Study Buddy project for music theory. The deck and its review record live at workspace/deck.json — each card carries its Leitner box and got-it/missed stats. The drill goes to workspace/drill.html and the follow-up plan to workspace/report.md.
setup.missionObjectives: Targeting is the whole point: the drill covers only what the record marks weak, with the numbers as evidence, and the plan schedules the way back. No live services, no real credentials.

success.summary: drill.html is a short interactive drill over only the record's weak material (intervals, key signatures); tasks/eval/report.md ranks the weak spots with numbers and schedules the follow-up.

checks.rubric: The drill items target only the material the review record marks weak (intervals and key signatures — box 1, missed-heavy); material the record marks strong stays out, and each item comes at the idea from a fresh angle rather than repeating a card verbatim.
checks.label: targeting

axes.name: targeting
axes.description: Every drill item traces to a card the record marks weak; strong material stays out — a generic whole-deck quiz misses the point.

axes.name: difficulty calibration
axes.description: Items come at the weak ideas from fresh angles at a level that stretches without drowning.

axes.name: encouragement
axes.description: Feedback coaches rather than scolds — right answers explained, misses met warmly.

axes.name: follow-up
axes.description: The plan restates the evidence, schedules re-runs and re-reviews, and defines when a spot counts as closed.
